correctness.rationale: For every odd p, subgroup inertia and two simple-pole ramification establish both genera; explicit norm/pullback base change gives Psi Phi=[p] with all cross terms zero; equality of dimensions makes Phi an isogeny and implies Phi Psi=[p]. Canonical adjunction gives pulled-back polarization p lambda and isogeny degree p^g; the kernel is a maximal isotropic finite subgroup scheme. Direct rational-point counting distinguishes the two Fp quotient Jacobians. Checker covers p=3,5,7,11 and quadratic extensions as corroboration only.

value.rationale: The canonical p-primary isogeny degree and polarization produce a full maximal-isotropic finite kernel scheme for every odd prime; those structural invariants are not determined by the unpolarized isogeny class. The two arithmetically distinct Fp quotient Jacobians and zeta numerator decomposition connect the structure to explicit rational-point counts across an infinite family. This is a natural integral arithmetic refinement, not merely a low-degree numerical observation.
